item.title: Missouri Basketball Rolls to Another Dominant Victory Behind Big Performances From Tiller and Crowe
item.description: Photo by: Denny Medley Tigers Set the Tone Early Missouri basketball continued its impressive run Friday afternoon, defeating Arkansas-Pine Bluff 97-61 at Mizzou Arena to earn its sixth consecutive victory. The Tigers entered the matchup looking to finish November on a high note before beginning a much more challenging stretch of their schedule. They accomplished that goal in convincing fashion, controlling the game from the opening minutes and showing their ability to dominate inside. Missouri wasted little time establishing its advantage. The Tigers opened the contest with an 11-0 run and eventually stretched their lead to 16-2 in less than five minutes. Arkansas-Pine Bluff struggled to find an answer for Missouri’s size and offensive pressure. The Golden Lions managed to settle down somewhat as the first half continued, but they never seriously threatened the Tigers’ advantage. Missouri continued attacking the basket, finding opportunities around the rim and creating quality looks through effective ball movement. Bryson Tiller was especially impressive during the opening half, scoring 14 points while making all four of his field-goal attempts. His production helped Missouri take a comfortable 51-28 advantage into halftime. Tiller Leads the Scoring Attack Tiller continued his strong performance throughout the afternoon, finishing with a team high 22 points, six rebounds, two assists and four blocked shots. The forward was difficult for Arkansas-Pine Bluff to contain, consistently using his size and athleticism to create scoring opportunities around the basket. His ability to contribute defensively also made a major difference. Jason Crowe Jr. delivered another impressive performance for the Tigers, finishing with 21 points. The freshman continued showing why he has become such an important part of Missouri’s offense, providing another reliable scoring option alongside Tiller. Mark Mitchell also made an important contribution in his return to the starting lineup. After missing time following a concussion, Mitchell finished with 14 points, three rebounds and three assists. Toni Bryant added 14 points, eight rebounds and four assists, giving Missouri another productive performance from its frontcourt. Missouri’s Defense Makes a Statement While the offense received plenty of attention, Missouri’s defensive performance was arguably just as impressive. The Tigers recorded 13 blocked shots, with Bryant accounting for a career high seven. Tiller added four blocks, helping Missouri make life extremely difficult for Arkansas-Pine Bluff around the basket. Missouri also forced 18 turnovers and recorded 12 steals. The defensive pressure prevented the Golden Lions from developing any consistent offensive rhythm. The Tigers finished shooting 57.6% from the field and scored 50 points in the paint. item.title: Seahawks’ Sam Darnold gets good news for NFC West clash with 49ers
item.description: Steven Bisig-Imagn Images Seahawks’ Sam Darnold gets good news for NFC West clash with 49ers appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Seattle Seahawks have a huge NFC West showdown on Sunday against the San Francisco 49ers. Sam Darnold has been out for the past two games due to quadriceps and rib injuries. However, the club’s latest injury report finally shares some good news for the 29-year-old quarterback. It’s said that Darnold is officially off the injury report , according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter. That means the nine-year veteran is finally returning from injury and is slated to get the start against the 49ers in Week 12. “Seahawks QB Sam Darnold is off the injury report and set to start Sunday vs. San Francisco,” Schefter reported. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) This will be Darnold’s eighth appearance this season, as he’s only missed three games so far this year. item.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua: The show before the show confirmed
item.description: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua is set for December 11 at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff, Wales. The entire event will be promoted by Queensberry Promotions, Matchroom Boxing, and Sela. Fight fans around the world will be able to catch that bout and three other undercard clashes live on Netflix. Recently, the main card was confirmed , with more fights added. Fight week just received a boost, with the announcement of a show on December 10, dubbed “ The Show Before The Show. ” This extra fight week card promoted by Gold Star Promotions will take place at Cardiff’s Vale Arena, with 12 fights for the event. Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua fight week receives boost The addition of this card gives the whole event a boost and provides a great opportunity for some fighters to get much-needed exposure. The December 10 event will be headlined by the excellent Australian Justis Huni (13-1, 7 KOs), who will face North London fighter Jeamie TKV (9-3, 5 KOs) for the Commonwealth title. Huni last fought on the Tyson Fury vs Arselanbek Makhmudov card, where he picked his spots well and impressed against a determined Frazer Clarke. Jeamie TKV also appeared on the same card, but lost his British title to Richard Riakporhe via a fifth-round stoppage. The rest of the card provides an opportunity for a plethora of talented fighters at different stages of their respective careers. The talented Welsh brothers, Garan and Ioan Croft, also appear on this card, as does an intriguing all-British middleweight dust-up between Sam Gilley and Brad Pauls. We will also bring you coverage of the Show Before The Show fight card. The Big Fight Weekend verdict Whatever you think about Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua and the fight night card, this December 10 card is an intriguing addition to fight week. The Croft brothers are talented fighters, and it’s great exposure for two young Welsh fighters to be involved in a fight week as big as this. Huni vs TKV is rightfully the main event, but what an opportunity for fighters like Ellis Panter and Ryan Jones to make a name for themselves. Sam Gilley vs Brad Pauls and Simon Ibekwe vs Tom Schwarz should also provide plenty of action

item.title: Patriots vs. Chargers predictions: Who will win the battle of the backups?
item.description: It’s time for a good old battle of the backups. In one corner, you have Tommy DeVito leading the New England Patriots offense in place of an injured Drake Maye; in the other corner, it’s D.J. Uiagalelei replacing Justin Herbert as starting quarterback for the Los Angeles Chargers. Who will win this marquee matchup? If the odds at FanDuel Sportsbook are to be believed, the Patriots: despite opening as 1.5-point underdogs, the line evolved over the week — first to 1.5 points in New England’s favor, and now to all the way to 3. So, let’s see what the Pats Pulpit staff and community think. Patriots vs. Chargers score predictions Bernd Buchmasser: Let’s be clear: the Patriots should win this game even with Tommy DeVito under center. The Chargers have been bad all season and on top of it all will be without Justin Herbert on Sunday; they also had two weeks to get ready for this matchup. That doesn’t mean this will be an easy win, because L.A. still has some good individual talent, but that if New England wants to remain a serious competitor for a playoff spot a games like this should leave no doubt regardless of the personnel available. | Patriots 20, Chargers 13 Patriots fans, join the game-day huddle! item.title: Recap: Wake Forest’s Comeback Effort Falls Short in 85-88 Loss to #24 Memphis
item.description: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - NOVEMBER 05: Kevair Kennedy #55 of the Wake Forest Demon Deacons looks on during the second half of the game against the Vanderbilt Commodores at Memorial Gym on November 05, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images In the final game of the Battle 4 Atlantis, the Deacs dropped their 2nd game of the season to the Memphis Tigers by a score of 85-88. Unbelievable fight falls just short. pic.twitter.com/MAGB94YP9e — Wake Forest Men's Basketball (@WakeMBB) November 27, 2026 The game started off fine for the Deacs, but after Kevair Kennedy picked up his 2nd foul just 6 minutes into the game, things fell apart rapidly. When Kennedy exited the game, the Deacs held a 13-8 lead with 14 minutes remaining in the half—Wake scored 13 points total in those final 14 minutes. Without Kennedy, the Deacs just don’t have a solid ballhandler who can run the offense, and the result was Wake’s worst half of basketball this season. The Deacs consistently initiated the offense 25 feet from the basket and could never get any penetration inside the 3-point line, so they spent a large portion of the half passing the ball around the perimeter and either turning the ball over or forcing up a bad shot before the shot clock went off. Wake finished the first half with just 26 points, shooting 8-19 from the floor (42%) and turning the ball over 12 times. The Tigers ended the half on a 17-4 run to take an 11 point lead at the break. Things continued that way until about the 8 minute mark in the 2nd half, after the Tigers went up by 20 points. Trailing 49-69, a switch was seemingly flipped in the Deacs, and they suddenly woke up and started playing basketball again. Behind 27 2nd half points from Kennedy, Wake outscored the Tigers 36 to 19 over the final 8 minutes of the game, and clawed back to as close a 1 point with 9 seconds remaining. Kennedy was suddenly getting to the rim at will, and the Deacs were able to force 9 Memphis turnovers by picking up full court and trapping the ball. 27(!) in the second half for Kev! https://t.co/x8jmiE3o6V pic.twitter.com/OY03aAqvRd — Wake Forest Men's Basketball (@WakeMBB) November 27, 2026 Ultimately, the comeback fell short as Kennedy tripped on the final possession of the game, but credit Wake Forest for not giving up. After playing 32 terrible minutes of basketball and getting behind by 20 points, it would have been easy to just concede and go hang out in the resort, but the team continued to fight until the very end. Wake ends the Battle 4 Atlantis 1-1 with a win over Mississippi State and a narrow loss to a ranked Memphis Tigers team. The Deacs definitely still have a lot to improve on if they want to play in the postseason, but I think this team is probably a lot better than many of us were expecting them to be this season. LSU is up next. Go Deacs!

item.title: Lions get good news despite brutal loss to Bears
item.description: Lions get good news despite brutal loss to Bears originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Detroit Lions didn't have much to celebrate on Thanksgiving after their brutal loss to the Bears . The team lost at home, which is always a stinger. But what made it worse is that the team was winning for most of the game. The game turned into a heated Thanksgiving Day matchup that ended with a 39-35 win for the Bears. In the final few moments, Rome Odunze and Caleb Williams connected for a game-winning touchdown that Lions fans would like to forget. But all is not lost. There's still a reason for Lions fans to be optimistic after their heart-wrenching loss. Lions still have reason to be optimistic despite heartbreaking Thanksgiving loss Dan Parr of the NFL's official website believes the Lions still have hope. "The Lions' dreams aren't dead, even after a gutting loss," he says in a postgame piece. The biggest reason the Lions should be happy is because their playoff probability is still an impressive 87% after the game loss to the Bears, according to Next Gen Stats. A lot of teams would love that. However, their chance of winning the division is now 28%. "Dan Campbell's crew will need to regroup now, but it's capable of doing so with one of the league's elite offenses. The Lions are looking up at the Bears in the division now, but they have won six of their last seven, and their next two games are against the Falcons and Titans , who have a combined record of 4-16," he says. So all is not lost, and the Lions' offense is certainly elite. But they're going to have to really close out games and not let another Thanksgiving Day nightmare happen. item.title: ‘He’s Been Awful,’ ‘Bo Nix Is Just Right-Handed Tua (Tagovailoa)’ — Shannon Sharpe, NFL World React to Broncos QB’s Performance in Loss vs. Steelers
item.description: ‘He’s Been Awful,’ ‘Bo Nix Is Just Right-Handed Tua (Tagovailoa)’ — Shannon Sharpe, NFL World React to Broncos QB’s Performance in Loss vs. Steelers Five points will get people talking, especially when your defense supplies two of them. The Denver Broncos’ 27-5 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers on Friday gave Shannon Sharpe plenty to complain about. Bo Nix finished with 169 passing yards, no touchdown passes, and three turnovers, and the criticism quickly spread from his decision-making to whether Denver can trust him in bigger games. An eight-win team arrived in Pittsburgh with a chance to strengthen its position in the AFC. Its quarterback left with a Tua Tagovailoa comparison nobody intended as a compliment. Shannon Sharpe Blasts Bo Nix’s Turnover-Filled Afternoon “[expletive] is BO doing? He’s been awful all [expletive] day. 🤬🤬🤬🤬🤬,” Sharpe wrote on X . The frustration had a pretty straightforward explanation. Nix completed 22 of 40 passes and threw two interceptions. He also lost a fumble that T.J. Watt recovered in the end zone, while Jalen Ramsey returned an interception 36 yards for another Pittsburgh touchdown. Denver’s offense failed to reach the end zone. Pittsburgh’s defense managed it twice, which is an awfully generous contribution to make to an opponent’s holiday weekend. BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN’s Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator Jon “Stugotz” Weiner supplied the comparison that summed up his assessment. “Bo Nix is just right-handed Tua,” he wrote . Zach Bye pointed to the difficulty Nix had producing downfield, citing his performance on throws traveling at least 10 yards. “Bo Nix 4 of 14 with two interceptions on passes thrown 10 yards or more down the field,” Bye wrote . “In the last two weeks, Nix has been outplayed by Fernando Mendoza in his first road start & Mason Rudolph off the bench. Not great.” Rudolph was making his first start of the season following Aaron Rodgers’ release. He finished with 142 yards and a touchdown on 9-of-15 passing, avoiding the giveaways that made Denver’s afternoon so miserable. He later walked back language he felt had become personal and said before Friday’s game that he had called Nix to apologize. item.title: Detroit Tigers’ Puzzling Beau Brieske Roster Move Suddenly Makes Sense
item.description: When the Detroit Tigers designated right-handed pitcher Beau Brieske for assignment on Friday afternoon, the move raised an interesting question. Why would the Tigers tender Brieske a contract for the 2027 season only to remove him from their 40-man roster a few days later? As it turns out, there may be a strategic reason behind the seemingly contradictory decisions. According to MLive Tigers beat reporter Evan Woodbery, the move could actually increase Detroit’s chances of keeping Brieske in the organization. Sep 22, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Tigers pitcher Beau Brieske (4) throws a pitch against the Washington Nationals in the ninth inning at Comerica Park. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Why the Detroit Tigers Designated Beau Brieske for Assignment The Tigers officially announced one-year contracts with Luis Gil and Ha-Seong Kim on Friday, designating Brieske and infielder Tsung-Che Cheng for assignment to accommodate the additions. However, Woodbery pointed out that Detroit previously used a similar strategy with outfielder Akil Baddoo. “Why DFA Brieske a few days after tendering him a contract for 2027?” Woodbery wrote on X . “Similar to what they did with Akil Baddoo a couple years ago: The tender could dissuade teams from claiming Brieske off waivers. If he goes unclaimed, he’ll be outrighted and become a well-paid Mud Hen.” Essentially, another team considering claiming Brieske off waivers would have to weigh the financial commitment associated with his tendered contract. That could make him a less attractive waiver claim, potentially allowing the Tigers to retain him in the minor leagues while freeing up a valuable 40-man roster spot. Could Beau Brieske Remain With the Tigers? Being designated for assignment does not necessarily mean Brieske’s time with the Tigers organization is over. If he clears outright waivers , Detroit could assign him to Triple-A Toledo, subject to his contractual and service-time rights. Of course, another organization could still claim Brieske, meaning there is some risk involved in the move. However, if Woodbery’s interpretation is correct, Scott Harris could ultimately free up a roster spot without losing a valuable pitching depth option. What initially appeared to be a head-scratching roster decision makes considerably more sense when viewed from that perspective.

item.title: Canucks Lose 3 Centers in Short Order: The Path Forward
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Vancouver Canucks centers are getting plucked and struck down one by one. Max Sasson has been traded , and then Elias Pettersson and Filip Chytil got hurt in the span of a week. Chytil was hurt in the latest game on Friday against the Philadelphia Flyers . Talk about bad timing for the team, as their depth will be greatly tested. Canucks Centers and Who Is Left? As it stands right now, Marco Rossi would be the undisputed number one center. Given his ice time and how Manny Malhotra has deployed him, it is not a good sign. However, it will be the best chance he will get to show his worth. Ty Mueller and Jacob Quillan have already been called up from Abbotsford and have played in the last four games for the NHL club. Paul Cotter and Drew O’Connor have played center this season for the Canucks, to mixed results. The Canucks will need to place either Elias Pettersson or Filip Chytil on injured reserve so they can call up an extra forward from Abbotsford. The Canucks could call up centers Riley Patterson, Akil Thomas , or Chase Wouters from the AHL. Patterson has the most points out of those three this season, with 11 points in 20 games for Abbotsford. Braeden Cootes has a reported hip injury, and the upcoming World Juniors championship is a priority. Therefore, he will likely not be the player called up in this situation. Centers to Keep an Eye On Marco Rossi stands out as the player to watch. If Chytil is out for an extended period of time, Rossi will be the first-line center. The question is, will Malhotra put him on the penalty kill? Chytil has played some PK minutes while Pettersson has been out. With just nine points in 28 games, there is no time like the present for Rossi to shine. If he does not, then questions will need to be answered. Ty Mueller is another center to watch. He has won 39 of 65 faceoffs (60%) in four games this season. His line alongside Drew O’Connor and Linus Karlsson has worked hard on the forecheck. He may be forced into a second-line role as the Canucks look thin up the middle. For Mueller, this may be the chance of a lifetime, and if he wants to carve out a role in the NHL, this is his time. item.title: Dolphins Target 31.5-Sack Edge Rusher For 2027 Draft
item.description: Credit: Scott Wachter-Imagn Images John Blair, writing for NFL Mocks, projects the 2027 NFL Draft’s third overall selection by the Miami Dolphins to be Texas edge rusher Colin Simmons, according to a report . This choice aims to fix a gaping hole on the defensive line that has cost the team games all season. Blair believes Simmons brings the specific burst and motor Miami needs right now. The Dolphins currently sit at a 1-9 record, tied for the worst mark in the league behind only the Titans and Chargers. That standing puts them in line for the third pick if the draft were held today. The team needs a difference-maker on defense, and Simmons fits that bill perfectly according to the projection. Blair noted that Simmons has the tools to become a dominant pass rusher who disrupts opposing offenses. Why Simmons Fits the Need Simmons has put up massive numbers at Texas this season and over his career. In just eight games this year, he recorded 10.5 sacks and 16 tackles for loss. His career totals across 37 games include 123 tackles and a staggering 31.5 sacks. These stats show he can get to the quarterback consistently, something the current Dolphins roster struggles to do. Current starters Chop Robinson and Josh Uche have shown flashes but lack the long-term consistency Miami requires. Robinson was a speed pick in 2024, yet his strength remains a weakness that opponents exploit. Uche is only on a one-year deal and has just three sacks this season. The team simply cannot rely on these two players to carry the pass rush for years to come. The Cost of a Thin Roster The need for a new edge rusher becomes even more urgent when looking at the injuries plaguing the defensive line. Three defensive tackles suffered season-ending injuries for the Dolphins prior to their latest matchup versus the Bills. With Zach Sieler, Jordan Phillips, and Zeek Biggers gone, the team is short on bodies and depth. Coach Jeff Hafley has called the recent defensive performance a “big team effort” because everyone had to step up. Defensive coordinator Sean Duggan praised the physical and mental shape of the players who played heavy snaps. Despite the praise, the roster is thin, and the coaching staff knows they need more help to survive the rest of the season. The Dolphins will face the New York Jets on Sunday, Nov. 29, at Hard Rock Stadium with a 1-9 record and a 3-8 opponent.

Chelsea suffered a third successive loss at the City Ground , with Alonso insisting everyone at the club must stick together during a difficult run of form. “We have to stick together,” he said. “Everyone that is in the changing room, everyone in the team is needed. We need to help and we need to go through this together. We don’t leave anyone apart. “We need to support everyone because we need everyone. We need the fans, we need all the players, we need to stick together because if not things will get more complicated.” Alonso also admitted Chelsea are struggling for confidence and solidity after another damaging defeat. “Many things didn’t go the way we wanted, for sure,” he said. “We are struggling to hold the result. We conceded the first goal. “Then once they scored the second, it was 2-1, there were minutes to play. So conceding the third one made it really, really difficult. “We are going through a difficult moment in solidity, in confidence, and we need to try to work to find solutions. “We need to find solutions to get back that confidence to play. And this is the only way.”

item.title: Jackson Koivun Doubles Career Earnings After Dramatic Win Over Brooks Koepka
item.description: | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Ajayi Segun Jackson Koivun has doubled his career earnings after winning the 2026 Farmers Insurance Skins Game at Atlantic Fields Club in Hobe Sound, Florida. The young American defeated Brooks Koepka in a closest-to-the-pin playoff on the 18th hole to claim the final skin worth $2 million. Koivun produced a better shot from 118 yards, with his ball finishing just inside Koepka’s. Koivun finished the event with $2.375 million after collecting four skins. The win gave him another big moment in a year that has already seen him make his mark on the PGA Tour. ALSO READ: Phil Mickelson Tips Jackson Koivun as Golf’s Next Big Star Jackson Koivun Beats Brooks Koepka for $2 Million The final hole produced the biggest moment of the competition after the value of the skin had carried over to $2 million. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Ajayi Segun Koivun, Koepka, Justin Thomas and Wyndham Clark were all in contention as the event reached its closing stages. The players could not settle the final skin during regular play, which meant the contest went to a closest-to-the-pin playoff. ALSO READ: Nick Faldo Calls on Former LIV Golf Stars to Help Pay Unpaid Suppliers Thomas and Clark failed to find the green with their shots. Koepka then hit his ball close to the hole, putting pressure on Koivun to produce something better. The 21-year-old responded with a shot from 118 yards that finished just inside Koepka’s. That was enough to give him the victory and the $2 million prize. Koivun had already won three other skins during the event, taking his total earnings to $2.375 million. Koepka finished with $700,000, while Thomas collected $475,000 and Clark earned $450,000. He turned professional after a standout college career at Auburn and quickly made an impression on the PGA Tour. Koivun claimed his first PGA Tour victory at the 3M Open in July , beating Scottie Scheffler by three shots. The win also helped him earn a place on the United States team for the Presidents Cup. He went on to finish the competition unbeaten, recording two wins and one tie. His performances have helped establish him as one of the young players to watch on the PGA Tour. The Skins Game gave Koivun another opportunity to compete against established players, and he made the most of it by beating Koepka in the final playoff. His $2.375 million payout also added a significant amount to his career earnings. Koivun will now look to build on his recent success as he continues his PGA Tour career. This will likely be the Heels’ toughest test so far, but this is also a bit of a different team from the one that played Georgia. Having Cameron Fens in the lineup has made a difference, and one would argue that Terrence Brown playing point guard in Neo Avdalis’ absence has had more of a positive impact on the team than a negative. The thing, though, is his ability to be a facilitator will be tested big in a big way tonight. The Mountaineers are currently averaging 8 steals per game, which is slightly higher than what Carolina has been doing. Having a team that is that active on defense when you do not have your starting point guard can be tough, so we’ll see if Brown is able to take care of the ball. On the flip side, West Virginia is also averaging 9.8 turnovers per game, which funny enough is also somewhat similar to UNC’s numbers. This game will ultimately come down to who can take care of the ball better and who will be able to rebound, but of course neither matter if the ball isn’t going into the basket. Given how aggressive the Heels have been in the paint — mostly because of the crazy stuff Brown has been able to do — it’s hard to see scoring being the big issue tonight. item.title: FSU beats South Carolina in PKs to advance to third round of NCAA Tournament
item.description: No. 5 seed Florida State women’s soccer defeated No. 4 seed South Carolina in penalty kicks (PKs) in the second round of the NCAA Tournament on Friday at Vanderbilt in Nashville, keeping their national championship defense alive. After a full 90 minutes and two 10-minute overtime periods, the teams remained tied at 1-1, forcing a penalty shootout that the Seminoles won 7-6. Competing in temperatures around 45 degrees, seven Seminoles played the full 90 minutes of regulation: Wrianna Hudson, Kate Ockene, Bridget Mutipula, Janet Okeke, Grace Hoytink, Nawreen Ahmad and Peyton McGovern. Six of those players remained on the field through both overtime periods, with Ockene exiting due to an injury early in the first overtime. South Carolina struck first in the 29th minute when Cuyler Zulauf found the back of the net, giving the Gamecocks a 1-0 advantage. Despite trailing at halftime, Florida State outshot South Carolina 6-2. However, both of the Gamecocks’ shots were on goal, while the Seminoles had yet to record a shot on goal. Florida State came out with renewed energy in the second half, finding the equalizer in the 55th minute when Okeke scored off a corner kick from Joelle Jung. The Seminoles continued to build momentum and apply offensive pressure, recording three corner kicks in the second half after having none in the first. Florida State nearly took the lead following a strong passing sequence that ended with Jung sending a shot over the crossbar. At the end of 90 minutes, the Seminoles had outshot the Gamecocks 17-7, with both teams recording three shots on goal. In the second minute of the first overtime period, Ockene went down with an injury. She was replaced by junior goalkeeper Fernanda Mayrink, who had made one start for Florida State this season. Mayrink made an immediate impact, stopping the ball following a South Carolina corner kick. She remained in goal for the remainder of overtime, recording a save. Florida State finished with 22 shots, including three on goal, but neither team was able to find the game-winning goal in either overtime period, sending the match to PKs. Nyanya Touray took Florida State’s first PK, but her attempt bounced off the post. South Carolina’s Ava Tutas converted her attempt to give the Gamecocks an early advantage. Hudson converted Florida State’s second attempt, followed by a successful PK from Zulauf to maintain South Carolina’s lead. Ahmad scored for the Seminoles before Reagan Schubach missed her attempt for the Gamecocks, evening the score at 2-2. Mayrink stepped up and converted her PK to give Florida State a 3-2 advantage, but Reese Slater responded for South Carolina. Lara Dantas converted for the Seminoles before Maggie Taitano answered for the Gamecocks, sending the shootout into sudden death with the teams tied at 4-4. item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. On Friday, Kuntz was already speaking of the team in the past tense. “I really enjoyed my time at the Galaxy. I love being here,” he said. “I’d like to be back if it was up to me. But it’s not.” Nor is it up to the team’s most loyal supporters, who would like to see someone sacrificed for the team’s fall from grace. item.description: Cavan Sullivan named MLS Young Player of the Year 🌟 Philadelphia Union and USMNT midfielder Cavan Sullivan has capped a record-setting regular season by being named the 2026 MLS Young Player of the Year. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. Tall turned to a scouting network led by Mark Nichols, bringing in a proven MLS veteran in Santi Rodriguez, Chile national team forward Gonzalo Tapia, securing a loan deal for Moroccan winger Anass Zaroury and signing designated player Brais Mendez, a Spanish attacker whose arrival from Real Sociedad brought to mind that of Cucho Hernandez. While Mendez is at a different stage of his carer than Hernandez was, he turned into a star in Columbus, showing his full potential in MLS after frustrating stints with Watford and loans in Huseca, Mallorca and Getafe. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Gotham FC’s home semifinal moved to 5K-seat stadium in field quality debacle
item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Corey Sipkin for the NY POST “At this level, in this kind of game, as a league, and we should have a better surface,” Amorós said. “Unfortunately, our club and football club did absolutely everything in their power to make sure that was the case. Unfortunately, it wasn’t. But luckily, it looks like nobody got hurt, and the game was what it was.” It’s not immediately clear if the NWSL penalized Gotham for a second consecutive week because of the field. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. Getty Images The head coaching role will take on an even bigger role going into 2027 as NYCFC prepares for massive changes with the planned move into their new stadium and MLS changing their league calendar to a summer-through-spring format, which is in line with the European football calendar and includes an abbreviated sprint season that will run from February to May. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. NYCFC will begin its search for a new head coach immediately, sporting director Todd Dunivant said in a statement released late Sunday morning. “We would like to thank Pascal for his commitment and contributions to New York City FC and wish him and his family all the best. This decision follows a thorough review of the season and reflects our ambition as an organization,” he said. One of the biggest problems that NYCFC faced this season – especially during its struggles in the second half – had been allowing late goals that would cost the club points, or matches altogether. And the club dealt with a number of injuries during the course of the season, while also playing much of the year without one of its top scorers, Alonso Martinez, as he recovered from a torn ACL he suffered last fall. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
